title: To Kill a Mockingbird
description: A Pulitzer Prize-winning novel set in the American South during the 1930s, told from the perspective of young Scout Finch. The story centers on her father, lawyer Atticus Finch, who defends a wrongly accused Black man in a racially divided town. It remains a standard text for secondary and university literature studies.

title: The Great Gatsby
description: An iconic portrait of the Roaring Twenties exploring wealth, obsession, and the elusive American Dream on Long Island. title: Animal Farm
description: A satirical political allegory portraying barnyard animals who overthrow their human master only to succumb to pig-led tyranny. The novella analyses power corruption, revolutionary ideals, and political rhetoric in accessible prose. Ideal for younger teens, high schoolers, and adult readers seeking sharp political fable.

title: Jane Eyre
description: A landmark Victorian bildungsroman tracing the life of an orphaned governess who asserts her moral independence and self-worth. Jane faces hardship at Lowood school and dark family secrets while working at Thornfield Hall. A foundational classic of English feminist literature and dramatic storytelling.

title: Wuthering Heights
description: A turbulent gothic novel set on the desolate Yorkshire moors recounting the destructive passion between Heathcliff and Catherine Earnshaw. The narrative explores revenge, social division, and generational cycles of trauma through multiple eyewitness accounts. Highly appreciated by fans of dark romance and classic Victorian drama.

title: Frankenstein
description: The pioneering nineteenth-century work that established modern science fiction and gothic horror traditions. Victor Frankenstein animates an artificial creature who is subsequently abandoned and seeks understanding from a hostile society. The text raises enduring philosophical questions on scientific ethics and human isolation.

title: The Kite Runner
description: A powerful contemporary novel exploring friendship, betrayal, and redemption set against the backdrop of Afghan modern history. title: Life of Pi
description: A Booker Prize-winning survival tale featuring an Indian teenage boy stranded in a lifeboat across the Pacific Ocean with a Bengal tiger. The narrative blends philosophical inquiry, faith, and zoological realism in a vivid survival story. Recommended for high school students and adult fiction readers.
